nfl.oneThing: The Eagles came back from 21 points down to beat the Cowboys 39–38 on Thanksgiving, the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history.

headlines.title: Eagles stun Cowboys 39–38 on Thanksgiving
headlines.summary: Philadelphia trailed 31–10 and still won at AT&T Stadium, with Jake Elliott kicking a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. Joe Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, and DeVonta Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards and two scores. Dallas had led by 21 points in the third quarter. The Cowboys then gave up a blocked punt for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, and Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal. Brian Schottenheimer defended his decision to go for it on fourth-and-1 from the Eagles' 39 with 55 seconds left. Dak Prescott was sacked, and the Eagles needed only 11 yards for the long field goal try.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia (4–7) is back in the NFC East conversation. Dallas (5–7) failed to win consecutive games again, and its path to the playoffs is now difficult at best. Jerry Jones said he doesn't expect a coaching change, but the pressure on Schottenheimer is up.

headlines.title: Caleb Williams and the Bears beat the Lions 39–35
headlines.summary: Chicago trailed by three late. On third-and-goal with nine seconds left, Caleb Williams found Rome Odunze in the back-right corner of the end zone for a 6-yard touchdown, and a brief review confirmed the catch. Williams threw for 345 yards and two touchdowns. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 205 yards and three touchdowns for Detroit, but the Lions lost anyway. Jared Goff threw for 313 yards, and Detroit's false start problems were a talking point after the game.
headlines.whyItMatters: Chicago (9–2) is the NFC's second seed and has won six straight.

headlines.title: Rodgers's rant leaves Steelers in turmoil
headlines.summary: Aaron Rodgers was benched for backup Mason Rudolph, then went on the Pat McAfee Show and criticised coach Mike McCarthy, including claims that McCarthy had slept through team meetings. The Steelers then waived Rodgers. Owner Art Rooney II said he was 'disappointed in where this went' and has '100% confidence in Mike McCarthy'. Mike Tomlin called the situation 'a dumpster fire', and Tom Brady said 'nobody wins when the family feuds'.
headlines.whyItMatters: Pittsburgh (6–4) is seventh in the AFC playoff picture. The team now has to get through the rest of the season without Rodgers on the roster.

nba.oneThing: The Spurs lost 116–111 at Portland despite 44 points and 16 rebounds from Victor Wembanyama, and host the Lakers on Friday in NBA Cup play.

headlines.title: Spurs fall 116–111 to Trail Blazers
headlines.summary: Victor Wembanyama scored 44 points with 16 rebounds and three assists, but Portland won. Deni Avdija scored 33 points with 12 rebounds and seven assists, and Damian Lillard added 29 points and five threes. Stephon Castle had 20 points and nine assists for San Antonio, and Devin Vassell had 18. The loss came before the Thanksgiving break and drops the Spurs to 15–4.
headlines.whyItMatters: San Antonio is second in the West and sits level on wins with the Lakers, who are 15–3 and first. Friday's game against the Lakers is a big one for the top of the conference.

headlines.title: LeBron's triple-double helps Sixers beat Heat 111–104
headlines.summary: LeBron James had 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds, his best game of the season. He scored 14 straight points in the second quarter as Philadelphia beat Miami in NBA Cup play. Jaylen Brown was ruled out for Friday's game against the Pacers with a left hamstring problem, and Joel Embiid is questionable with an illness. Friday's win would clinch Eastern Conference Group B and send the 76ers to the NBA Cup knockout rounds for the first time.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia (15–4) is first in the East. Brown has now missed two games in a week with the same hamstring problem, which makes his availability for the rest of the NBA Cup a concern.

headlines.title: Durant reaches 33,000 career points in Rockets win
headlines.summary: Kevin Durant became the fifth player in NBA history to reach 33,000 career points as Houston beat Phoenix 116–104. Alperen Sengun had 23 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists. Durant had 20 points and 10 rebounds. The night also included an exchange with Dillon Brooks, who was ejected after the two went nose-to-nose late in the game.
headlines.whyItMatters: Houston (14–5) is fourth in the West. Phoenix (9–8) is tenth, after a loss to the Rockets.
